TASK: Advisory-only deep-dive (read-only, NO file edits, return analysis as text) on three data-plane details of a Windows-first Tauri client for a low-latency remote-desktop protocol. Protocol: TCP via TLS-PSK (openssl crate, external PSK with identity strings, TLS1.2 PSK ciphersuites), UDP datagrams AES-256-GCM (12B nonce = 4B prefix + 8B big-endian counter, direction-separated HKDF keys, 4096-packet sliding replay window), video = HEVC AVCC-style (4-byte big-endian length-prefixed NALUs, VPS/SPS/PPS prepended to keyframes), 60fps target, ~16ms decode-to-pixel budget.

DELIVERABLE — exact API-level design + edge cases for each:
1. openssl crate TLS-PSK CLIENT on Windows: rust-openssl API surface for PSK client callback, which TLS1.2 PSK ciphersuites to pin, identity string handling (UTF-8 bytes vs null-termination), vendored-openssl build implications on Windows CI (openssl-sys features, perl/nasm, prebuilt options). Assume no Schannel fallback.
2. Replay window port: incoming nonce embeds 8-byte big-endian counter; window = counter within 4096 below highest, duplicate bitmask per 64-block. Design the Rust struct for SPSC use, nonce prefix role, confirm counter reuse across reconnects is safe with per-session fresh keys.
3. HEVC decode pipeline: ffmpeg-next (libav) — hevc decoder with AVCC extradata (set extradata to VPS/SPS/PPS blob, feed length-prefixed NALUs) vs per-frame AnnexB conversion; hardware accel on Windows (d3d11va hw_device_ctx) vs software fallback; frame pacing for ~16ms decode-to-present; decoded frames into wgpu texture (D3D11 shared texture zero-copy vs staging copy — quantify 4K30 copy cost).

VERIFY: exact crates/APIs/versions; flag uncertainty as UNCERTAIN with verification path.
STOP WHEN: all three sections delivered.
Advisory-only analysis for planning — not implementation.
